rv.q: If you think that “wiping away tears of laughter and sorrow” is one those activities that, like “rolling in the aisles”, only happens in reviews, you give should this show a visit.
This joyous, cathartic musical looks set to see out many calendars.

The reason I say this comes from the unique way that this musical has been developed. Not only has the show been co-created by Tim Firth and Gary Barlow, but you get the firm impression that this is a writing partnership that works together in an altogether unusual way.
With all the arguments and upheaval currently in the world, The Girls is a heart warming tonic.
Yet The Girls also blossoms into a feel-good hit as bright as a field of sunflowers.

The score is very pleasant and moving if not lacking a little pace. The standout vocal performance for me was West End Wilma Award Winner Claire Machin's display of rasp and sass in a big high-energy number in Act 1. Claire Moore plays a brilliant Chris, cheating her way through the baking competition with a jam sponge from M&S.

cn.t: This heartfelt musical adaptation of Calendar Girls earns warm reviews for its fresh, joyous approach to familiar material, with Barlow and Firth's poignant songs elevating the story beyond a simple rehash.
